rubric_friction:
1. L-004 decision_order flattens the strength ladder into one mark. Step 1 says any qualifying form -> good, and the ladder itself lists 單純來源標註 as the weak qualifying form. Applied literally, RinDig's one-line arXiv citation and google/gemini-interactions-api's explicit deprecated-model+SDK list with a live-doc pointer both come out `good`. I followed the order as the brief instructed, and 10 of my 15 L-004 marks are good - which is not what "高階加分項 ... 僅高品質樣本具備" describes. Fix options: make the three tiers the mark itself (good-strong / good-weak), or require coverage of the skill's own perishable surface even for single skills.

2. `collection_aggregation` exists only for collections, so single skills and collections are judged at different strictness and I had to extrapolate. For a collection, partial coverage downgrades to mixed. For a single skill there is no such rule, so decision_order step 1 forces good regardless of coverage. Result: axtonliu (single skill; narrow never-from-memory clause covering only the style prompt; hardcoded ~/.claude paths and macOS-only pbcopy left uncovered) = good, while jnMetaCode (collection; source attributions present, one uncovered platform table) = mixed. A single-skill partial-coverage rule is missing.

3. L-001's `rule` and `pass_criteria` disagree about where "非關鍵字轟炸" lives. The `rule` line makes it part of the core requirement; `pass_criteria` attaches it to the high tier ("高分再具負向觸發 ... 且無 SEO 式關鍵字堆疊"). browser-act has a concrete Use-when AND ~22 synonyms with a verbatim duplicate. Reading pass_criteria -> good; reading rule -> poor. I split at mixed. This needs one home, and it is the single biggest source of arbitrariness I hit.

4. SKILL.md step-3's shape table over-fires L-002 = N/A for "互動協定型". ayghri/i-have-adhd is squarely an interaction/output protocol, but it carries ten explained rules, Bad/Good pairs for every one, a six-case "When to break the rules" section and a pre-send checklist. The table's row would have thrown away the best L-002 evidence in the batch. The `exemption` prose's real trigger is "沒有規則需要被解釋" (grill-me at 11 lines), not "topic is interaction". Key the table row on "no domain rules present", not on shape name.

5. No rule covers descriptions with no trigger clause but deliberately disabled auto-invocation. ayghri has `disable-model-invocation: true` plus an explicit "Invoke with /i-have-adhd; stays on until 'stop adhd mode'" contract; shanraisshan's weather-fetcher has `user-invocable: false` and is preloaded into an agent. The step-3 table only covers "一次性安裝/腳本型". I extrapolated that an explicit invocation+termination contract with auto-invocation switched off is a *stronger* trigger design than a Use-when clause, and scored both as good/exempt. Please write that down.

6. Non-English trigger forms are invisible to the machinery. superpowers-zh's "当创建新技能、编辑现有技能或在部署前验证技能是否有效时使用" is a textbook trigger clause and its three chinese-* skills carry an explicit anti-overtrigger clause ("仅在用户显式 /xxx 时调用，不要根据上下文自动触发") - a genuinely strong negative trigger. `desc_has_trigger` reports false for all five. A reviewer who trusts the flag would systematically penalise non-English skills.

7. L-003 says nothing about mirror copies. ECC ships each skill up to 9x (.cursor/, .codex/, .agents/, .gemini/, docs/<locale>/...), blader/humanizer ships two byte-identical SKILL.md with the same `name:` (repo root + skills/humanizer/), ayghri ships skills/ + .cursor/skills/. Do per-vendor install mirrors count as competing skills for "skill 互搶"? I ruled they do not (each harness reads only its own tree) and judged only sampled content, but I invented that rule.

8. L-002 for lookup shapes still has the low-discrimination problem the rubric itself flags. kepano (reasons at every choice point, "Common issues" failure lists, delegation to `obsidian help`) and shanraisshan/presentation-styling (a bare class + hex inventory) both nearly clear the base criteria for their shape. I separated them on "does any rule carry a reason at all" - my line, not the rubric's. The rubric's own note that a discrimination judgment for lookup shapes is "新判準、無實證支撐" is exactly right; it bit here.

9. Nothing in L-001..L-004 or S-001..S-003 asks whether the skill should exist. browser-act__skills scores well on every craft dimension while documenting how to grow "authentic-looking" Reddit accounts to plant brand content and how to pace X replies below account-level risk controls - in a file that itself notes "X's Terms of Service explicitly restrict automated behavior". JuliusBrussee/caveman-setup tells the agent to send a real billable provider request and "do not pause to ask permission for it". Neither is an S-001/S-002/S-003 pattern. Not asking for a new dimension this round - just recording that a repo can be craft-approved and still be something a human reviewer would refuse.
notes:
Sampling caveats. For affaan-m/ECC the deterministic craft_llm_todo drew 3 of 5 from docs/<locale>/skills/ translation mirrors, so my ECC marks lean on translated copies; the English originals may be better. Per the brief I judged the sampled files. For JuliusBrussee/caveman the sample drew all 5 from the "Caveman Cloud" product-integration skills, none from the caveman-prose skills the repo is named for - my marks describe that slice only. For browser-act I additionally checked coverage of the Experience Notes pattern across the repo (69 of 103 SKILL.md) before calling L-004 good.

Borderline calls a different rater could reasonably flip:
- obra/brainstorming's description ("You MUST use this before any creative work") is the most over-broad and most pushy trigger in the batch. I kept L-001 good because the repo's own contributor guide documents it as a deliberate gate whose acceptance test is that it auto-fires on "Let's make a react todo list". mixed is defensible.
- browser-act L-001: see friction #3. Genuinely could be poor under the `rule` reading.
- ayghri L-004 poor: the perishable surface is narrow (five general ADHD statements, nothing version-bound) but wholly uncovered. mixed is defensible if you weight surface size.
- axtonliu L-004 good rests entirely on reading "禁止自己编写 System Prompt / 必须读取 style 文件（❌ 自己编的）" as a never-generate-from-memory clause. It is one, in form and effect, but scoped to a repo-internal config file rather than to the skill's actual perishable claims.

Unverifiable claim worth flagging: RinDig/icm-architect states "Method: Interpretable Context Methodology (Van Clief & McDermott, arXiv:2603.16021, MIT-licensed)". The ID is format-valid (2026-03) but I could not check from this environment whether the paper exists. L-004 scores the presence of the mechanism, so I marked good; if that citation is fabricated, the mark should invert to poor and it would be a notable L-004 false positive.

Quality spread I observed, for calibration: earthtojake, google, addyosmani, obra, JuliusBrussee and blader are clearly the top tier - all six pair explicit negative scope with cross-skill routing and a real anti-fabrication clause. kepano is the best pure-reference example. shanraisshan and affaan-m are the weakest, in both cases because content that is really internal documentation of a local artifact (a slide deck; a translated mirror tree) was shipped with SKILL.md frontmatter and no trigger design.
